docs.title: About
docs.text: Skip to content Leiðarljós is a guiding light. Leiðar is the genitive of leið , a way or course. Ljós is light. The compound is the lamp you keep on a path. The binary is ljos . Why it is not the first line The door teaches the first success: write one claim, search it back. A stranger does not need the Icelandic before that works. The name stays on the brand, the lamp mark, and this page. What the lamp is for The seat writes only on Remember: and Prefer: . Nothing is mined from chat. A sitting opens the pack, the island, and the ticket. Finish writes what the work produced. That is the path the name points at. Pronunciation Approximate English: LAY-thar-lyohs . Icelandic ð is the voiced th in this . ljos is the same word without the path. First write: /docs/start/ . Handbook: /handbook/ .

docs.title: Compare
docs.text: Skip to content What packset measured packset is the standing-knowledge store in the seat. It writes only on Remember: and Prefer:. The crate explanation holds the rows. Neighbouring systems are named by protocol. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference What we measured LongMemEval_S (doi:10.48550/arXiv.2410.10813), 470 answerable questions, session-level retrieval. The pack writes claims, not harvested chat. Reproduction: scripts/longmemeval_qa.py and docs/orgmode/results/longmemeval-s-qa.org in packset. Arm hit@1 recall@5 recall@10 packset BM25+ 0.855 0.914 0.952 packset fused panel 0.889 0.949 0.981 Answer accuracy on the same 470 uses a local 7 B reader and judge (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q5_K_M, LongMemEval prompts, top five sessions). CombMNZ fusion is 0.549. Lexical alone is 0.532. Labelled sessions, the ceiling for any retriever, are 0.634. MemoryAgentBench (doi:10.48550/arXiv.2507.05257), reader Qwen2.5-7B. Accurate retrieval scores each source on its own metric, then takes the mean of the four. Lexical job 11759 is 0.568 (95% CI 0.530-0.605, clustered by question). The per-source scores are SH 0.730, MH 0.530, LongMemEval (S*) 0.370 and EventQA 0.640. Published rows are BM25 0.605 and HippoRAG-v2 0.651 with a GPT-4o-mini reader. Conflict resolution at 262K is 0.395 for fused live (job 11750, CI 0.350-0.440) and 0.240 for lexical. The published FactConsolidation rows are BM25 0.255 and HippoRAG-v2 0.295. Hop2 (job 11793) is about 0.555 from the job log, with its verdicts held out. Neighbouring published numbers Two public repositories share the name agentmemory. They report different protocols. The first is session retrieval (R@5). The second is question answering with a hosted generator and a hosted judge. packset publishes both a retrieval row and a local-reader QA row so those protocols stay distinct. System Protocol Published figure Write policy rohitg00/agentmemory LongMemEval-S retrieval, R@5, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 95.2% (their COMPARISON.md) Lifecycle hooks capture transcript text JordanMcCann/agentmemory LongMemEval QA, hosted generator and judge 96.20% on 481/500 (their README) Chat over a MemoryStore packset LongMemEval_S session retrieval; QA with a local 7 B reader recall@5 0.949 fused, 0.914 lexical; QA 0.549 against a 0.634 labelled ceiling Remember: and Prefer: only The 0.949 fused recall@5 is the neighbour of the 95.2% R@5 retrieval figure. The 96.20% QA figure uses a different generator and a different judge. InjecMEM and MINJA describe the risk of writing from a transcript. packset writes only on Remember: and Prefer:. Privacy-of-write . What the other habitats answer Retrieval is one store. The seat also cites frozen product, the tracker, this-session claims, argv law, and weighted agreement. Those questions are not retrieval scores. Question Store What did the human freeze? cards What does this seat know, standing? packset What did this unit produce? deedar What does this node stand on, and who agrees? vissue What is this session handing out? claimdag May this argv run? ljos-policyd Who is right, under trust? ljos-consensus policyd is argv law ljos policy -- argv prints the line and any pack rule that matches it. ljos rule writes that law into the pack. ljos-policyd is the TCB when it is on PATH or POLICYD_BIN : it prints allow or deny. Reloading a pack is not a check. ljos-policyd docs · Argv field note . Source: packset explanation · packset

Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference ljos The seat over the stores. crate packset Standing knowledge. Remember: and Prefer: only. crate deedar Frozen product. Opened by accession. crate vissue The file is the database. Graph and agreement. crate claimdag This-session claims. Remember and Prefer stay in packset. crate The loops, drawn The memory loop: a write enters the review clock; recall and the hook read it; graded reschedules it; a rewrite closes the earlier claim. The handover: satchel, atoms and deeds sealed and signed; the receiver verifies before it imports, and refuses one altered byte. Steppers and the fold Steppers. docs.title: Harnesses
docs.text:
Skip to content Wire ljos-mcp One entry for any runner. The seat names itself after the client that connects, and the shell finds the same name; nothing is set per runner. ljos and ljos-mcp on PATH is the whole install. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference One entry, any runner $ ljos onboard { "mcpServers": { "ljos": { "type": "stdio", "command": "/home/you/.cargo/bin/ljos-mcp", "args": [], "env": {} } } } $ ljos protocol > instructions.md Paste the entry where the runner keeps its MCP servers. Every runner that speaks MCP over stdio takes this shape, and there is nothing to fill in: the env is empty on purpose. Put the protocol where the agent reads its instructions; the server serves the same text at ljos://protocol and names it in its instructions, so a runner that loads neither skills nor resources still reads it first. Who is sitting The seat does not know the runners. It knows one thing every runner does: it connects, and says its name. ljos-mcp takes that name at initialize as the seat and leaves a record under the runtime directory keyed by the runner's process. ljos in a shell the runner opens walks its own process tree to that record, or, when the runner has no MCP, to the first ancestor that is not a shell, and names the same seat. A runner's tools and its verbs are one seat with nothing set; a new runner needs no table anywhere. $ ljos seat seat acme-cli holder acme-cli-39u source the server the runner opened, process 4242 Two names come from that. The seat is the program: memory, ballots and trust rows accrue to it across every conversation of that runner, which is what calibration needs. The holder is the seat tagged with the conversation's process, and it is what a claim is held under; occupancy is holder:issue , so two conversations of one runner hold two tickets and a second sitting does not release the first. With several agents open in one terminal workspace, every pane is one process, so every conversation is one holder and the same program stays one seat. A server and its shells share the runner's process and not its environment, which is why the name is read from the process and not from a session variable: a line editor's session id in the shell had made one conversation two holders, and every sitting met held by another seat . ljos doctor carries the same row; LJOS_SEAT overrides the seat when a person wants a name. A hook, when the runner has one If the runner has a command hook on prompts, pipe the prompt to ljos hook . The memories it activates come back as context, preferences first, each once per session, with once a session how many claims and habits are due. Do not add it on every tool call to search the pack: a turn issues many tool calls and one prompt. On a tool call the hook applies the TCB ( ljos-policyd ) and then the pack's rules, and a deny blocks. The seat guards its own law Before any rule, the hook refuses a command or a file edit that writes the seat's binaries ( ljos , ljos-mcp , ljos-policyd ), its config, the approval store, or a runner's hook registration ( ~/.codex/hooks.json , ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json , ~/.claude/settings.json , ~/.grok/hooks/ljos.json ); reading them is fine. An agent the gate refused had replaced ~/.local/bin/ljos with a script that allowed everything, which also broke every other runner's prompt hook. ljos doctor fails its seat binary row when the ljos the hooks run is not the binary running the doctor. An ask on a runner that cannot ask prints a request id. The person grants that one command, once, in that directory and conversation, with ljos approve ID in a terminal of their own; approve refuses under an agent runner or without a terminal, so an agent cannot grant itself consent. A runner with a register command A runner that registers servers by a command of its own, or reads them from a config file, can be described once in ~/.config/ljos/harnesses.toml and onboarded in one verb. ljos onboard --example prints the shape; --dry-run reports and writes nothing. [[harness]] name = "runner-a" register = ["runner-a", "mcp", "add", "-s", "user", "ljos", "--", "{server}"] registered = ["runner-a", "mcp", "get", "ljos"] skills = "~/.runner-a/skills" hooks = "~/.runner-a/settings.json" [[harness]] name = "runner-b" config = "~/.runner-b/config.toml" marker = "[mcp_servers.ljos]" snippet = "
[mcp_servers.ljos]
command = "{server}"
args = []
" skills = "~/.runner-b/skills" $ ljos onboard --harness runner-a ok host key /home/you/.config/deedar/host.key exists ok runner-a mcp ran runner-a mcp add -s user ljos -- /home/you/.cargo/bin/ljos-mcp ok hook memory hook: add it on UserPromptSubmit in /home/you/.runner-a/settings.json ok skill wrote /home/you/.runner-a/skills/ljos/SKILL.md {server} is the path to ljos-mcp . Nothing about the seat's name goes in the table. A runner whose hooks file maps a hook name to its events, and whose payload does not name the event, takes hooks_named : the seat writes its hooks under that name, each command told its event with ljos hook --event . Antigravity's agy is one: ljos onboard --harness antigravity registers the server in ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json , writes the skill under ~/.gemini/config/skills , and puts the gate on run_command , the notes on each model call and the stop audit in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json . That runner asks the person on an ask itself. [[harness]] name = "antigravity" config_json = "~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json" json_pointer = "/mcpServers/ljos" json_entry = '{"command": "{server}", "args": [], "env": {"LJOS_SEAT": "{name}"}}' skills = "~/.gemini/config/skills" hooks = "~/.gemini/config/hooks.json" hooks_named = "ljos" The two verbs an agent runs ljos sitting <issue> # doctor, cards, due, island, recall, timeline, claim ljos finish <issue> --lesson "..." [--outcome <option>] # remember, fire, complete, learn One verb opens a sitting in the protocol's order and stops at the first store that does not answer. One closes it. The loop that makes the seat a memory runs every time. It does not wait for someone to remember the steps. Cite a deed on a ticket ljos evidence deed-… ljos deed <id> --add deed-… ljos recall <id> Citing a deed names it; the bytes stay in deedar. The ticket stays open until vissue closes it. Share the seat across machines ljos sync --key # this machine's age public key cat .ljos/sync.toml # in the tracker repository name = "work" recipients = ["age1…", "age1…"] # the machines allowed to read it ljos sync # take the others' logs, write this one's Memory travels with the tracker repository. Each machine writes one sealed log under .ljos/atoms/ , and only the named recipients can open it. The sitting takes the other machines' logs before it walks the island, and finish writes this machine's. A lesson takes the scope of the repository its issue lives in; a [projects] table in sync.toml sends one project's lessons to another scope. Merge the tracker by heading vissue merge-driver --install # in each clone of the tracker git add .gitattributes && git commit -m "chore: merge issues.org by heading" Two hosts that edit one issues.org merge by issue, not by line: notes and ballots from both sides are kept, and a state both sides moved takes the later logged move. A field both sides changed some other way keeps yours and is written on the issue as a merge-conflict note. ljos doctor fails the tracker row in a clone that lacks the driver. Let Jev judge, where a machine allows it ~/.config/ljos/jev.toml enabled = true key_cmd = ["pass", "show", "api/typesafe/jev"] Jev is TypeSafe's decision model: it answers yes-or-no, choice and score questions with probabilities, and writes no text. With the file above, three judgments go to it. The prompt hook asks which of up to ten claims bear on the prompt and whether the prompt corrects the agent or puts a choice; the local cross-encoder is then never loaded. ljos vote --as NAME --jev and ljos panel --jev ask for persona ballots, cast one when Jev

docs.title: The island
docs.text: Skip to content The cluster this task touches. A persona is a view over everything. An island is the linked claims this piece of work involves. Overview Install Island Open a ticket Crates Fig. 1 landfold of the live seat pack: 148 atoms (74 lesson, 12 preference, 60 persona, 2 trust). 384-D bge-small, landfold embed --dot --fun-hd asinh,0.56 --center , stress 0.021. Cream is the pack. Gold is the docs activation island; rings are seeds. Fig. 2 the same 148 atoms, folded from the link graph: pairwise distance is 1 − weight on an edge and 2 off-edge. landfold embed --similarity --fun-hd asinh,0.5 --center , stress 0.075. Hop-PHATE stacked 148 points onto 44 positions; this fold keeps 148 unique. Gold is the docs activation island. How it is built The pack links each claim to the claims it shares names with. Those links form clusters. ljos island TASK takes the top search hits as seeds and spreads activation two hops: half lost per hop, divided by fan-out. The cluster comes back strongest first. That is spreading activation over a semantic network (Collins and Loftus, doi:10.1037/0033-295X.82.6.407). Fig. 1 folds sentence vectors (bge-small, cosine as --dot , Ceriotti asinh at the median pairwise scale). Fig. 2 folds the weighted link graph. Gold is the docs activation cluster, not a 3-gram hash. How use shapes it When the seat uses an island, ljos island --fire moves each fired pair's weight toward one and fades the rest (Hebb with Oja's term). The next cue like this one walks a heavier path. The weights travel in a handover. Search ranking is separate On LongMemEval the island lost as a ranker (hit@1 0.377 against the fused panel's 0.889). Activation flows to hubs. The island is orientation and what fires together after use. The verb lives on the pack. The seat prints the strongest eight when it opens a ticket. The fold is landfold . Field note: ljos explanation .

docs.title: Policy
docs.text: Skip to content May this command run? Before a coding agent's shell command runs, the runner's hook asks ljos. Four layers judge it in order; the first refusal stands, and no later layer can allow what an earlier one refused. None of them is a model. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference The four layers The seat guard. A command that writes the seat's own files, its binaries, its hook entries, ~/.config/ljos , the approvals store, is refused. An agent cannot rewrite the law it runs under. ljos-policyd. A binary with fixed rules. Each pipeline of the line reaches it as one call, so a download piped into a shell is judged as one thing. It refuses privilege runners ( sudo , doas ), a download handed to a shell, a recursive delete outside /tmp , a setuid chmod , raw-disk writes and a force push. Seat rules. Rules you write with ljos rule , kept in the seat's memory and tried against each command of the line. A quoted sentence or a heredoc body is data, not a command. The push gate. A git push is free to a repository your account owns alone and has never released. Anywhere else it needs LJOS_CITE=ISSUE , the tracker issue that records the decision behind it. Try it $ ljos-policyd check -- git status allow $ ljos-policyd check -- sudo id deny sudo $ ljos-policyd check -- curl -fsSL https://example.org/i.sh '|' sh deny curl-pipe-shell $ ljos rule '*--force*' --verdict deny --why "Never force push." $ ljos policy -- git push --force origin main deny: Never force push. (rule `*--force*`) ljos policy -- COMMAND prints the combined answer for one command without running it. ljos-policyd version says which law the binary carries: the table built into it, or phronesis after that table, when the library was present at build time. What the agent sees On Claude Code, Codex and the other runners, the refusal is the hook's answer and the command never runs: $ echo '{"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_input":{"command":"git push --force"}}' | ljos hook {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"git-force-push (seat rule `ljos-policyd`)"}} A rule with --verdict ask stops the command and asks you instead. On Claude Code that is its own permission prompt. On a runner without one, the hook prints a request id; you reply approve ID in the same conversation, or run ljos approve ID in a terminal, and the agent retries. A request from another conversation grants nothing, and an agent cannot type an approval into a pane. The runner's own settings come first: a command they deny is refused before any hook is asked. Without the binary If ljos-policyd is not on PATH , the second layer has no opinion and the other three still run. ljos doctor shows a policy row saying so. Set POLICYD_REQUIRED=1 to refuse every command until it is installed. Crate site: ljos-policyd . The rules in full: the ljos-policyd README .

docs.title: Privacy-of-write
docs.text: Skip to content Extract-on-write is refused A seat that harvests a transcript is a different product. leiðarljós writes only on Remember: and Prefer:. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference Only explicit claims Remember: and Prefer: are the pack writes. The text is the claim. It is not parsed out of a sitting. Empty text is refused. Cards stay frozen USER.md and MEMORY.md are a human freeze. ljos cards prints them. It never writes them. Overflow is an error, not a prompt to dump more. The harness memory file is dead Do not write a client memory file and call it standing knowledge. The pack is the pack. The cards are the cards. Citing a deed names it An accession can be named in more than one habitat. Each habitat keeps its own store. Opening the bytes is a deed question. Jev sends text off the machine With ~/.config/ljos/jev.toml on, the prompt, up to ten of the pack's claims, a persona's brief, or a stopping turn's request, commands, latest output and final message go to TypeSafe's API. Nothing is sent without that file and enabled = true on the machine. Leave it off where company data must stay on the machine. The ticket stays open ljos complete finishes a session node. The cited ticket stays open until the tracker says otherwise.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Skip to content CLI and MCP ljos is the seat. Habitats keep their own CLIs. The ticket stays open until vissue closes it. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference CLI Verb Habitat Does ljos sitting ID seat Open: doctor, cards, due, island, recall, timeline, claim. ljos finish ID seat Close: remember, fire, complete, learn. The ticket stays open. ljos remember TEXT packset POST one explicit claim. Needs PACKSET_URL . ljos prefer TEXT packset Same write path, kind preference. ljos search QUERY packset Retrieve standing knowledge. ljos evidence ACCESSION deedar Frozen product bytes. ljos current ACCESSION deedar Current pointer. ljos deed ID [--add ACCESSION] tracker Cite. The bytes stay in deedar. Crate: vissue. ljos recall ID tracker Working set. ljos vote ID [--for CHOICE] tracker Ballots. ljos claim NODE claimdag This-session CAS. ljos complete NODE claimdag The ticket stays open. ljos hook policyd, pack On PreToolUse: TCB then pack rules; a deny blocks. On a prompt: pack text. ljos cards cards Read USER.md / MEMORY.md . Never writes. ljos policy -- ARGV policyd TCB then pack rules. A deny blocks. A check is the argv verdict. ljos consensus ID consensus crate DeGroot / ODE, then the tracker verb. MCP ljos-mcp execs ljos . Tool names match the verbs, including ljos_vote . Tool Arguments Does ljos_remember text Standing knowledge. Never extract-on-write. ljos_prefer text Standing preference. Never extract-on-write. ljos_search query Retrieve via PACKSET_URL . ljos_evidence accession deedar evidence. ljos_current accession deedar current tip. ljos_deed issue , optional add Cite an accession on a tracker node. ljos_recall issue Working set. ljos_claim node Claim a claimdag node. ljos_complete node Complete a claimdag node. The ticket stays open. ljos_cards — Read-only cards. ljos_policy argv TCB then pack rules. A deny blocks. A check is the argv verdict. ljos_consensus id ljos-consensus then the tracker verb. The settle is the consensus. Install the seat cargo binstall ljos Crate sites: ljos · packset · deedar · vissue · claimdag · consensus · ljos-policyd

docs.title: Sit and finish
docs.text: Skip to content Open a ticket. Print the island. An island is the cluster of linked claims this task activates. The ticket stays open until vissue closes it. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference 1. Point at scratch stores A first sitting should not touch a live tracker. Make an empty tracker directory, export the roots, start the pack writer, and ask doctor. A tracker is a directory holding Software/ or a vissue.toml . $ mkdir -p /tmp/seat/tracker/Software && cd /tmp/seat && git init -q $ export VISSUE_ROOT=/tmp/seat/tracker DEEDAR_URL=file:///tmp/seat/deeds $ export CLAIMDAG_DIR=/tmp/seat/claims PACKSET_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18761 $ packsetd --port 18761 --home /tmp/seat-pack & $ ljos doctor 2. Make a ticket and sit it sitting prints its sections in order and stops at the first store that does not answer: doctor, sync, cards, due, the island the title activates, open blockers, the playbook it binds, the panel when the issue is a decision, recall, timeline, then the claim. Sync pulls the tracker and takes the other machines' sealed memory logs before the island is walked. On a decision issue the panel section writes one brief per persona the title names; each brief starts a subagent that casts one ballot as that persona, and finish --close refuses a decision with fewer than two ballots. When the tracker is a git checkout, the claim is committed and pushed, so another host sees who holds the ticket. After the sitting, read each due row and run ljos graded ID (or --lapsed ). The clock does not move until you grade. --assignee is for a named worker. Left off, or given as a pronoun ( you , seat , agent ), the holder is this conversation's: the seat tagged with its process, the same in the runner's tools and its shells ( ljos seat prints it). Occupancy is holder:issue , so two conversations do not share one slot and a second sitting does not release the first. $ id=$(vissue create -p demo "Ship the fuse change?" -q) $ ljos sitting $id == doctor ... == timeline ... == claim gen=2 3. Cite what the work produced A deed is frozen bytes. The ticket cites the accession. Citing a deed names it; the bytes stay in deedar. $ echo 'fn main() {}' > patch.rs $ deedar create file --name "the fuse patch" --path patch.rs --agent you $ ljos deed $id --add deed-file-the-fuse-patch 4. Finish The lesson is remembered. The island fires. The session node completes. An outcome, when named, rewrites trust. The tracker issue is still open until someone closes it there. When the tracker is a git checkout, finish commits the ticket's file and pushes it; the last line says so. A closure that stays in one working tree does not exist for any other host. $ ljos finish $id --lesson "The fuse patch shipped as one file. Nothing else moved." remembered ... completed the session node ... as done tracker git: committed and pushed chore(issues): ... finished Agreement is ljos consensus over ljos-consensus on crates.io. The seat crate walks the same loop: ljos getting started . Field note: completing is not closing .

docs.title: First write
docs.text: Skip to content Write one claim. Search it back. A reader who has never used the seat finishes this page with one lesson in the pack. Search returns the same text. A review clock is running on it. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference 1. Install $ cargo binstall ljos packset Without cargo-binstall , cargo install ljos packset is the same. Other runners: Harnesses . Work starts as a ticket. vissue q -p PROJECT "TITLE" mints it in the tracker VISSUE_ROOT names, and ljos sitting claims it. That tracker is yours. A ticket filed on one machine is invisible to every other install until VISSUE_ROOT is a git checkout those machines share. The sit page uses a scratch tracker under /tmp so a first run does not touch a live one. 2. Write one claim, then retrieve it $ ljos remember "the default fuse is CombMNZ" 8e3e7827... lesson due 2026-10-10T21:56:09.549Z the default fuse is CombMNZ $ ljos search fuse Score is how the scorers ranked this query. ... 1.0000 3/3 lesson 8e3e7827... today the default fuse is CombMNZ ljos remember starts the writer when none is answering. PACKSET_URL=off is the one way to have no pack. A URL pointed somewhere else is not replaced. 3. The clock $ ljos due 0 due; 1 scheduled, next at ... Search shows kind lesson and the same sentence. A review is scheduled a day out. Tomorrow ljos due lists the claim. ljos graded ID (or --lapsed ) moves the clock. 4. Prefer is the same path $ ljos prefer "never extract on write" $ ljos search extract Score is how the scorers ranked this query. ... 2.0000 3/3 preference fe9d4d04... today never extract on write 1.0000 1/3 lesson 8e3e7827... today the default fuse is CombMNZ The fraction is how many of the scorers named the hit. Neither number says whether the claim is true. Next: sit and finish . The crate tutorial runs memory, agreement, and a handover: ljos getting started .

docs.title: The pin is an accession.
docs.text: Skip to content The pin is an accession. Back to the field DEEDAR_URL names the directory ( file:// plus a path). Unset, the command has nowhere to write. deedar create file needs --id , --path , and --agent . The pin is deed-… or sha256: . ljos evidence asks deedar for the bytes. ljos deed ID --add ACCESSION names the accession on a ticket. The product stays in deedar. The pack may name the same accession. Each habitat keeps the name. If the store is empty, that is an error. Frozen product / deedar

docs.title: The settle is the consensus.
docs.text: Skip to content The settle is the consensus. Back to the field ljos vote ID --for OPTION records a ballot. One ballot per identity; --as NAME casts as a persona. A recast replaces. A missing identity is no. ljos consensus ID is the seat verb: the model crate, then the tracker, both under the trust rows the pack holds that apply to the issue's topic and every persona's anchor. The model is DeGroot / Friedkin–Johnsen, or bounded confidence when the issue is tagged broad , or the Seldon ODE when --seldon and seldon are on PATH. Every outcome says how the group split, in polarization and disagreement; a count says only who won. On a hard question add a forecast beside the ballot, ljos predict ID --expect OPTION ; with two or more forecasts the settle also names the surprisingly popular answer, the option whose actual share most exceeds its forecast, and shows each voter's standing from the rows. The rows are memory. ljos learn ID --outcome OPTION weighs each voter by its record's accuracy, shrunk toward the panel's pooled accuracy, keeps the outcome, and loosens the anchors of refuted personas; ljos calibrate -p PROJECT writes rows from the project's history when nobody names an outcome; ljos trust FROM TO W --about DOMAIN sets one by hand, scoped. ljos consensus discounts the voters who err together once five issues have an outcome. Under equal rows a settle is a count. A panel is one subagent per persona, each started from ljos brief NAME ID , each casting one ballot as itself, then the settle. ljos persona NAME --anchor A --view TEXT --about DOMAIN writes the persona once; it stays in the pack. Where the machine turned Jev on, ljos panel ID --jev asks Jev for each persona's ballot first. Jev returns what the ballot always carried and a subagent had to guess: the chosen option's probability is the confidence, and its forecast of the panel is the prediction, so the settle and the surprisingly popular reading need nothing new. Personas answered by one model are one correlated voter, so the panel casts only when every seat is sure (confidence 0.8 or above) and all agree. Otherwise it casts nothing and writes the briefs, and the subagents take the contested question. learn scores a Jev ballot like any other. Four green ticks are a host rule for landing work. They are not the model. Do not report a count as if it were the crate. The explanation is where a settle's claim comes from: the closed form the iteration solves for, the round count guaranteed for an anchored settle, the SymPy check and the interval enclosure under Derivations, proofs and certificates, and when to use each model. consensus · ljos · seldon-code

docs.title: A check is the argv verdict.
docs.text: Skip to content A check is the argv verdict. Back to the field $ uvx ljos-policyd check -- uv run pytest allow $ ljos-policyd capnp -- true | wc -c 40 The typed verdict is Cap'n PolicyDecision (phronesis; Ali Akber Saifee / indynull, HaoZeke). A Janet pack can deny more after that verdict: (defn check [argv] (when (has-prefix? (get argv 0) "sudo") (deny "sudo"))) ljos-policyd check -- argv is the TCB when the binary is on PATH (or POLICYD_BIN ). It prints allow or deny . capnp writes the packed message. The harness hook and ljos policy call it. The Janet pack may only deny more. ljos policy -- argv prints the line, then the TCB verdict if the binary answered, then any pack rule that matches, then what the pack knows that bears on it. The binary prints a verdict. Pack rules stay in packset. A missing binary leaves the line open unless POLICYD_REQUIRED=1 . Doctor names the row. ljos hook on PreToolUse is the same gate. A deny is a blocked tool call: $ echo '{"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_input":{"command":"git push --force"}}' | ljos hook {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"git-force-push (seat rule `ljos-policyd`)"}} On a prompt it searches and holds pack text; PostToolUse emits it. Nothing to say on a prompt is no output. A TCB deny still blocks. ljos onboard installs it on a runner's tool-call and prompt events. When the session ends, the memories the hook injected during it fire together, so what served one sitting is wired for the next. Law can live in the pack: ljos rule 'PATTERN' --verdict deny|ask --why "..." writes a glob over the command line with a verdict, and the hook returns it as the runner's permission decision while ljos policy prints it beside the line. A rule is memory: dated, supersedable, exported in handovers. A pack rule is tried on the whole line and on each command the line runs. The line splits on && , || , ; , | and & outside quotes, and leading NAME=value assignments and sudo , env , time , nohup come off, so cd repo && git push meets git push* and a commit message that names a command does not. A pattern that says re: , or carries \b , \s , \d , \w or an alternation group, is a regular expression anchored at the command's start. Edit a pack rule only when argv law itself changes. Do not write comments, dates, ticket ids, or sitting notes into it. If the binary is down, leave the pack rules alone. Other projects may speak one habitat and ignore ljos . Habitats · Compare

docs.title: Overflow is an error.
docs.text: Skip to content Overflow is an error. Back to the field ljos cards prints USER.md and MEMORY.md from --dir (default . ). A missing file prints nothing. The command never creates those files and never writes them. Cards answer one question: what did the human freeze? Overflow is an error, not a prompt to dump more. A client scrapbook is not a card. Read the cards at the start of a sitting. If they are empty, leave them empty. Habitats

docs.title: The ticket stays open.
docs.text: Skip to content The ticket stays open. Back to the field ljos sitting ISSUE [--assignee NAME] opens the sitting: doctor, cards, due, island, recall, timeline, claim, in that order, stopping at the first store that does not answer. The name defaults to this conversation's holder, the seat tagged with its process ( ljos seat prints it); a named worker passes its own. Occupancy is holder and issue: one live claim per holder per issue. A second claim is refused with the issue the name still holds and the two verbs that free it: ljos complete finishes it, ljos release hands it back unfinished. ljos finish ISSUE --lesson "..." [--outcome OPTION] closes the sitting: remember, fire the island, complete, learn. A later sitting on the same issue reopens its node and takes it; the ledger keeps the earlier completion. The ticket stays open until vissue closes it. The tracker is the graph. Create and claim tickets through vissue . Never hand-edit issues.org . Crate docs: vissue.rgoswami.me . File before you speak. An audit with no ids is unfinished work. A leftover that does not fit this sitting is a child ticket, then the original work continues. Session work / claimdag

docs.title: Remember is a speech act.
docs.text: Skip to content Remember is a speech act. Back to the field ljos remember POSTs one lesson to /v1/atoms . ljos prefer POSTs one preference. The writer is found on 127.0.0.1:8761 with nothing set; packset ensure starts one. A writer that is down is an error, never an empty pack. The seat's memory is one workspace, seat , from any directory. The pack's own command line keys a workspace to the git remote of the directory it stands in; the seat does not, because a seat is one memory across every repository it works in. PACKSET_WORKSPACE names another on purpose. Search is GET /v1/search on the seat's workspace. It does not open a deed. A transcript is not a source. If you did not say Remember: or Prefer: , the pack did not change. Every recalled memory carries its age ( [lesson, 3 weeks ago] ), and the hook's lessons run oldest to newest behind the preferences; read them as a timeline, a later one revises an earlier one. ljos timeline ISSUE is the tracker's logbook, the cited deeds and the activated memories as one dated list, oldest first, with the gap between lines. ljos search TOPIC --as-of TIME is the pack as it stood then. A lesson that rewrites an earlier one (same opening words, a new object) closes the earlier one's window on arrival, and remember says so. ljos consolidate runs the same rule over what is already held and reports the pairs; --apply closes them. Run it after ljos receive --import . ljos island CUE is what a task touches; ljos hubs is what the pack turns on by its own links, a weighted PageRank over them: the natural list to pin, to review first, or to carry when the whole pack is too much. Every claim enters the review clock on write. ljos due lists what is due and ends with one line on the clock; ljos graded ID moves it. A claim never graded sinks in search as its retrievability falls. If packset status says up and remember hangs or returns 400, the writer is wedged. packset stop , then packset ensure . Do not dump the sitting into a card. Privacy-of-write

docs.title: Write one claim. Search it back.
docs.text: Skip to content Write one claim. Search it back. ljos is memory, a work tracker and a shell-command gate for coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. It writes one claim when you say Remember: or Prefer:, then searches that claim back. Nothing is mined from chat, and memory stays on your machine unless you turn on a remote judge. Write one claim How sitting works Source Fig. 1 A sitting, in the order ljos prints it. The ticket stays open until vissue closes it. specimen sitting remember policy $ ljos sitting demo-k29f == doctor == sync == cards == due == island == blockers == playbook == recall == timeline == claim gen=2 install Copy cargo binstall ljos packset ljos remember "the default fuse is CombMNZ" ljos search fuse ljos remember starts the writer when none is answering. The walk: First write . The name: leiðarljós . The loop Write. Sit. Finish. 01 Remember One claim, two sentences at most, stored as written. ljos remember and ljos prefer are the only pack writes. Nothing is mined from a transcript. 02 Sit ljos sitting opens: doctor, sync, cards, due, island, blockers, playbook, recall, timeline, claim. Cite what the work produced. The ticket stays open until vissue closes it. 03 Finish ljos finish remembers the lesson, fires the island, completes the session node, and learns from an outcome when one is named. Words: a seat is one agent runner on one machine, with its memory and claims. A sitting is one piece of work on one ticket. A deed is a hashed record of what that work produced. packset is the memory store, and vissue is the tracker, plain Org files in git. leiðarljós is Icelandic for a guiding light. Fig. 2 LongMemEval_S, n = 470 answerable questions, session retrieval. CombMNZ fuses BM25+ with multilingual-e5-large; the default install encodes with bge-small-en-v1.5, and without the encoder search stays lexical. Writes only on Remember: and Prefer:. arm recall@5 QA / ceiling BM25+ lexical 0.914 — CombMNZ fused 0.949 0.549 / 0.634 QA uses a local 7 B reader and judge, top five sessions, against the labelled-session ceiling.
